change.author: Gabe Villalobos

findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` calls `timezone.now()` when the class body runs. Every `AssignmentSource` built without an explicit `queued` (including `from_integration`) gets the process start time, not the time it was created. The field is meant to record when the assignment was queued, so the value is wrong and gets staler the longer the process runs. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

findings.title: Tests can't catch the stale `queued` default
findings.body: `test_to_dict` only asserts that `queued` is not None, so it passes with the import-time default. Add a test that two instances created at different times get different `queued` values (for example by freezing time). Also fix the typo in the name `test_from_dict_inalid_data`.

contracts.action: Pass assignment_source through assign/deassign to the outbound assignee sync task and skip sync when the source integration is the target
contracts.equivalent_path: Existing sync_group_assignee_outbound passed only external_issue_id, user_id and assign to the task
contracts.before_after: The new path adds assignment_source_dict to the task kwargs. The task parses it with from_dict and passes it to should_sync, which returns False when the integration ids match. It also passes assignment_source to installation.sync_assignee_outbound; the Jira, VSTS and Example implementations accept **kwargs, so this is safe.
contracts.visible_effect: Assignments that came inbound from an integration are no longer echoed back to the same integration. Other integrations still sync.
contracts.failure_mode: A malformed dict makes from_dict return None, so the sync proceeds without cycle protection. This fails open and is not visible to the user.

summary: The cycle-prevention change is sound, and the existing outbound implementations accept the new kwarg. One real bug: `AssignmentSource.queued` defaults to `timezone.now()` evaluated at import time, so it is stale. The tests don't catch it.
